subject: key expansion length
value: 10 clocks, one round key per clock (key_cnt 1..10), the first in the row after the start row
reason: Spec only says the expansion runs serially before decryption; a serial design with one 4-word step per clock gives 10 steps. Spec does not give a count.

check.rows: update case rows 1..10; first decrypt step in row 11

subject: initial AddRoundKey
value: a separate clock (round_cnt = 1) with rk[10]; no InvShiftRows/InvSubBytes in it
reason: Spec lists it as its own step ('Initial step'); one clock per step is the simplest serial reading.

check.signal: state register after first decrypt clock
check.rows: update row 12 / no-update row 2 equals ct ^ rk[10]

subject: one clock per decryption round, total latency
value: rounds 1..9 and the final round take one clock each; o_done row = 22 (update) / 12 (no update), counted from the start row = 0
reason: Not fixed by the spec; the TB/cocotb accept any latency (wait for o_done). Chosen as the minimum for a registered, serial design.

check.rows: row 22 (update), row 12 (no update); compare the round counter row by row

subject: o_done shape
value: registered one-cycle pulse; 0 in the row after the start row; 0 again in the row after it
reason: TB waits for a rising edge of o_done, and cocotb stops at the first sampled 1; a stale 1 would break both. A held-until-next-start o_done would also pass if cleared by the start edge; pulse chosen.

check.rows: rows 1 and done+1 are 0; exactly one row is 1

subject: o_data when o_done = 0
value: o_data is the state register directly (no separate output register); intermediate values are visible while busy; 0 after reset
reason: Spec fixes only o_data when o_done = 1 and (cocotb) after reset, where the library model starts with decrypted_data presumably 0 (the library harness_library is not visible; assumed 0).

check.rows: row after reset = 0; row with o_done = 1 = plaintext; other rows free

subject: reset values
value: all registers 0: key_cnt, round_cnt, o_done, key_done, state, stored round keys; reset also forgets the stored key
reason: cocotb resets 4 times and always starts the first run with update_key = 1, so the stored key after reset is never used; the spec says nothing else.

subject: start while busy / in the done row
value: start while key_cnt != 0 or round_cnt != 0 is ignored; start in the o_done row is accepted (idle then)
reason: Not stated. cocotb starts the next run in the row after o_done has been seen; TB starts at least one row later. Neither starts while busy.

check.rows: not exercised by TB/cocotb; only check the design does not restart a running operation if this is tested

subject: capture of i_data and i_key
value: both captured at the start edge (i_data into state_reg, i_key into rk[0] when i_update_key = 1)
reason: TB and cocotb set both to 0 in the row after start, so the design must have stored them.

check.rows: row 1 equals the ciphertext (state) and the key (rk[0], update case)

subject: start without update right after reset
value: not defined; model uses rk = 0 (key 0 not expanded)
reason: Spec silent; never exercised (first run after every reset is update = 1).

subject: i_update_key sampling
value: looked at only in the start row (start_with_update vs start_without_update); never remembered beyond that except through key_cnt/round_cnt
reason: TB and cocotb clear it in the row after start, as the task text's own prompt lists it as the start modifier ('asserted by i_update_key and i_start').

check.signal: i_update_key and the signal that selects key expansion
check.rows: update case rows 1..10 (i_update_key = 0 there, expansion must still run)

subject: round key order in decryption
value: initial AddRoundKey rk[10]; rounds 1..9 rk[9]..rk[1]; final round rk[0]
reason: Not written in the task text; follows FIPS 197 (inverse cipher) and the expected value of the TB vector.

subject: key_done as an internal signal
value: key_done = 0 from reset and from the start edge of an update; 1 from the end of key step 10; stays 1 later
reason: The name and meaning are the architect's; the spec only requires 'expand first, then decrypt'. An RTL may encode this differently (for example a counter only).

check.rows: update row 11 first 1; no-update case 1 in all rows

subject: stored key form
value: all 11 round keys are kept; a no-update run does not re-expand
reason: Task text: 'the stored expanded key'. If the RTL stored only the cipher key and re-expanded each time, the no-update latency would be 22, not 12.

check.rows: no-update case: no key_cnt activity in rows 1..11

subject: byte order of i_key and i_data/o_data
value: byte 0 = most significant byte, row n%4, column n//4
reason: Fixed by the TB comment for i_data and by the TB vectors for the key and output (expected plaintext 3243f6a8... is the FIPS vector); listed so the RTL map can confirm it.

check.signal: load of state_reg and of rk[0]

subject: internal control signals upd_load, start_accept, key_cnt, round_cnt
value: named and split as in model.json (upd_load = idle & i_start & i_update_key; start_accept = idle & i_start)
reason: Spec has no internal signals; an RTL may merge them in one FSM, use other encodings or one-hot state. The HDL map may mark a block as 'merged' if the function is the same.

check.rows: compare values per row with the schedule, not names

subject: add_round_key input mux
value: add_round_key.state comes from state_reg.q at round_cnt = 1 and from inv_sub_bytes.state_out at round_cnt = 2..11; the mux is counted with round_mux
reason: The initial AddRoundKey skips InvShiftRows/InvSubBytes. An RTL may instead apply those and bypass them with a mux, or add a separate initial XOR; the function per row is what counts.

check.signal: input of the XOR with the round key

subject: round key store read for the key step
value: rk_prev = rk[key_cnt-1] is a combinational read of the registered store; the new key is written at the end of the same row
reason: Serial one-key-per-clock schedule (AA1). An RTL may keep only the last round key in a working register and the finished keys in the array.

check.rows: update rows 1..10 each hold the next round key one row later

subject: latency numbers in ports_detail
value: combinational ports 0 cycles, registered ports 1 cycle; cumulative rows per case in schedule
reason: Consequence of AA1-AA4; any other register placement changes the numbers.

subject: model_cli argument encodings
value: rk_all = rk[0]||...||rk[10] (rk[0] most significant, 352 hex digits); counters as hex numbers; round_mux CLI only selects a path
reason: Needed for rtl blockcheck; the RTL array may use another index order, then the HDL engineer must map it (and say so).
